lem-qftx-parametric-vector-bundle-sectio:
## Statement

Let $X$ be a compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold, $K\subseteq X$ a closed smooth submanifold with a chosen collar, $M$ a compact smooth manifold, and $E\to M$ a finite-rank smooth real vector bundle. Let $s:X\times M\to E$ be a continuous family of sections, meaning $s(x,m)\in E_m$ and $(x,m)\mapsto s(x,m)$ is continuous. Assume $x\mapsto s(x,\cdot)$ is continuous in the uniform topology, its restriction to $K$ is continuous in the $C^\infty$ section topology, and for distinct marked points $m_1,\ldots,m_q\in M$ the values $s(x,m_i)=v_i\in E_{m_i}$ are independent of $x$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a family $\widetilde s:X\to\Gamma^\infty(E)$ continuous in the $C^\infty$ topology, equal to $s$ on $K$, equal to $v_i$ at every $m_i$, and satisfying $\sup(\{0\}\cup\{\|\widetilde s(x,m)-s(x,m)\|:(x,m)\in X\times M\})<\varepsilon$ for any fixed bundle norm. The straight-line homotopy in each vector fiber from $s$ to $\widetilde s$ fixes $K$ and all marked values.
def-qftx-mapping-cone-hopf-invariant:
## Definition

Let $f:S^3\to S^2$ be a based continuous map. Give $S^2$ an orientation and give the attached $4$-cell its chosen orientation. Its mapping cone is the CW complex $C_f=S^2\cup_fD^4$, with the basepoint as its $0$-cell. Let $x\in H^2(C_f;\mathbb Z)$ be the unique class restricting to the positive generator of $H^2(S^2;\mathbb Z)$, and let $y\in H^4(C_f;\mathbb Z)$ be the generator determined by the oriented $4$-cell. Define the integral mapping-cone Hopf invariant $H(f)\in\mathbb Z$ by the equation
$$x\smile x=H(f)y.$$
def-qftx-suspension-pinch-map:
## Definition

Let $(Z,z_0)$ be a based topological space. Define its reduced suspension as $\Sigma Z=(Z\times[0,1])/(Z\times\{0,1\}\cup\{z_0\}\times[0,1])$, with the collapsed subset as basepoint. Let $\iota_1,\iota_2:\Sigma Z\to\Sigma Z\vee\Sigma Z$ be the wedge inclusions. The reduced suspension pinch map $p_Z:\Sigma Z\to\Sigma Z\vee\Sigma Z$ is induced by
$$p_Z([z,t])=\begin{cases}\iota_1([z,2t]),&0\le t\le\tfrac12,\\\iota_2([z,2t-1]),&\tfrac12\le t\le1.\end{cases}$$
At $t=\tfrac12$ both values are the wedge basepoint.
lem-qftx-hopf-generator-and-cone:
## Statement

Let $h:S^3\to\mathbb{CP}^1\cong S^2$ be the Hopf map $h(z_0,z_1)=[z_0:z_1]$ on the unit sphere in $\mathbb C^2$. Then $h$ generates $\pi_3(S^2)\cong\mathbb Z$. Use the integral mapping-cone Hopf invariant $H(f)$ defined for based maps $f:S^3\to S^2$ by $x^2=H(f)y$ in $C_f=S^2\cup_fD^4$, with the positive degree-two and oriented top-cell generators. With the complex orientations, $C_h\cong\mathbb{CP}^2$, $H(h)=1$, and for every integer $m$ and degree-$m$ map $d_m:S^3\to S^3$, $H(h\circ d_m)=m$.
lem-qftx-folded-product-attachment-suspe:
## Statement

Give $S^2\times S^2$ its product CW structure with $2$-skeleton $W=S^2\vee S^2$ and one oriented $4$-cell attached by $\alpha:S^3\to W$. Let $\nabla:W\to S^2$ fold the two oriented summands by the identity and put $\beta=\nabla\circ\alpha$. For a based map $f:S^3\to S^2$, its integral Hopf invariant $H(f)$ is defined by $x^2=H(f)y$ in the mapping cone $C_f=S^2\cup_fD^4$, where $x$ and $y$ are the positive generators of $H^2(C_f;\mathbb Z)$ and $H^4(C_f;\mathbb Z)$. With the product orientation, $H(\beta)=2$. Moreover the suspension $\Sigma\beta:S^4\to S^3$ is nullhomotopic. Consequently, if $\eta_3=\Sigma h$ is the suspension of the Hopf generator, then $2[\eta_3]=0$ in $\pi_4(S^3)$.
lem-qftx-suspended-hopf-composite-adem-o:
## Statement

Set $\eta_2=h:S^3\to S^2$ and $\eta_j=\Sigma^{j-2}h:S^{j+1}\to S^j$ for $j\ge2$. For every $n\ge2$, the composite $\eta_n\circ\eta_{n+1}:S^{n+2}\to S^n$ is not nullhomotopic.
lem-qftx-special-unitary-column-fibratio:
## Statement

For each integer $N\ge2$, let $SU(N)=\{U\in M_N(\mathbb C):U^*U=I,\det U=1\}$ and let $p:SU(N)\to S^{2N-1}\subset\mathbb C^N$ send a matrix to its last column. Then $p$ is a smooth, locally trivial fiber bundle with fiber $SU(N-1)$ over the last standard basis vector; for $N=2$, the fiber is the one-point group $SU(1)$.
lem-qftx-low-unitary-homotopy-inputs:
## Statement

For every $N\ge2$, $SU(N)$ is path connected, $\pi_1(SU(N))=\pi_2(SU(N))=0$, and $\pi_3(SU(N))\cong\mathbb Z$. In addition, $\pi_4(SU(2))\cong\mathbb Z/2$ is finite and $\pi_5(SU(2))\ne0$. Here $SU(2)\cong S^3$ by the map sending a unit quaternion to its defining special-unitary matrix.
lem-qftx-pi5-special-unitary-nonzero:
## Statement

For every integer $N\ge2$, $\pi_5(SU(N))$ is nonzero. The claim is only nonvanishing; no full computation of these groups is asserted.
lem-qftx-parametric-gauge-smoothing:
## Statement

Let $M$ be a compact connected oriented boundaryless smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension $d\in\{3,4\}$, let $N\ge2$, let $P\to M$ be a smooth principal $SU(N)$ bundle, and fix a frame $p_m$ over $m\in M$. Use the adjoint group bundle $Ad(P)=P\times_{Ad}SU(N)$. Write $\mathcal G_\infty(P)$ for the smooth gauge group with its $C^\infty$ section topology as defined from finite-atlas derivative seminorms, and set $\mathcal G_{\infty,m}(P)=\{u\in\mathcal G_\infty(P):u(p_m)=e\}$. Define $\mathcal G^0(P)$ as the group of continuous sections of $Ad(P)$ with the compact-open topology and $\mathcal G^0_m(P)=\{u\in\mathcal G^0(P):u(p_m)=e\}$. Then the inclusions $\mathcal G_\infty(P)\hookrightarrow\mathcal G^0(P)$ and $\mathcal G_{\infty,m}(P)\hookrightarrow\mathcal G^0_m(P)$ induce bijections on path components and isomorphisms on all homotopy groups at every basepoint. More precisely, finite sphere/disk parameter families and their relative homotopies have the same classes in the smooth and continuous section topologies.
lem-qftx-sphere-gauge-evaluation-fibrati:
## Statement

Let $P\to S^r$ be a smooth principal $SU(N)$ bundle with $r\in\{3,4\}$, $N\ge2$, a chosen point $m\in S^r$, and a chosen frame $p_m$ in its fiber. Write $\mathcal G(P):=\mathcal G_\infty(P)$ for the smooth gauge group defined by the finite-atlas $C^\infty$ section topology, let $\mathcal G_m(P):=\{u\in\mathcal G_\infty(P):u(p_m)=e\}$, and put $\overline{\mathcal G}(P):=\overline{\mathcal G}_\infty(P)=\mathcal G_\infty(P)/Z_N$, where $Z_N$ is the finite subgroup of constant central gauge sections. Evaluation $ev_m(u)=u(p_m)$ gives a locally trivial bundle
$$\mathcal G_m(P)\longrightarrow\mathcal G(P)\xrightarrow{ev_m}SU(N),$$
and the quotient map $\mathcal G(P)\to\overline{\mathcal G}(P)$ is a finite covering. For a local section $s:U\to\mathcal G(P)$, the bundle chart has the commutative form
$$\begin{array}{ccc}\mathcal G_m(P)\times U&\xrightarrow{\Phi_s}&ev_m^{-1}(U)\\\downarrow{\operatorname{pr}_2}&&\downarrow{ev_m}\\U&\hookrightarrow&SU(N)\end{array}$$
where $\Phi_s(v,g)=v\,s(g)$; the square commutes because $ev_m(v)=e$ and $ev_m(s(g))=g$. The corresponding TikZ source is:
```tikz
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal G_m(P)\times U \arrow[r,"\Phi_s"] \arrow[d,"\operatorname{pr}_2"'] & ev_m^{-1}(U) \arrow[d,"ev_m"]\\
U \arrow[r,hook] & SU(N)
\end{tikzcd}
```
The evaluation bundle is numerable; both maps are Serre fibrations and have the homotopy long exact sequence.
lem-qftx-based-gauge-sphere-homotopy:
## Statement

Let $P\to S^r$ be any smooth principal $SU(N)$ bundle, where $r=3$ or $4$ and $N\ge2$. Fix a frame over a point $m$ and write $\mathcal G_{\infty,m}(P)=\{u\in\mathcal G_\infty(P):u(p_m)=e\}$ for the based subgroup of the smooth gauge group defined by finite-atlas $C^\infty$ derivative seminorms; for brevity put $\mathcal G_m(P):=\mathcal G_{\infty,m}(P)$. For every $j\ge1$ there is a group isomorphism
$$\pi_j(\mathcal G_m(P),e)\cong\pi_{j+r}(SU(N),e),$$
and there is a bijection of pointed component sets $\pi_0(\mathcal G_m(P),e)\cong\pi_r(SU(N),e)$. These identifications are independent of the clutching class of $P$; the unbased evaluation fibration may still depend on that class.
thm-qftx-reduced-gauge-group-sphere-nont:
## Statement

Let $r\in\{3,4\}$, $N\ge2$, and $P\to S^r$ be any smooth principal $SU(N)$ bundle. Write $\mathcal G(P):=\mathcal G_\infty(P)$ for its smooth gauge group with the finite-atlas $C^\infty$ section topology and $\overline{\mathcal G}(P):=\overline{\mathcal G}_\infty(P)=\mathcal G_\infty(P)/Z_N$ for the quotient by constant central gauge sections. Then either $\overline{\mathcal G}(P)$ has more than one path component or at least one of its based homotopy groups $\pi_j(\overline{\mathcal G}(P),e)$, $j\ge1$, is nonzero. More precisely, for $r=3$ it has infinitely many path components, and for $r=4$ its fundamental group is nontrivial.
lem-qftx-section-retract-obstruction:
## Statement

Let $p:E\to B$ be a nonempty locally trivial principal topological $H$-bundle with right $H$-action, and suppose it has a continuous section. For any $b_0\in B$, the fiber $H$ is a retract of $E$. If $E$ is weakly contractible, then $H$ is path connected and $\pi_j(H,e)=0$ for every $j\ge1$.

The retraction is expressed by the commutative diagram
$$\begin{array}{ccc}H&\xrightarrow{i}&E\\\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle\operatorname{id}_H}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle r}\\H&=&H\end{array}$$
with TikZ source
```tikz
\begin{tikzcd}
H \arrow[r,"i"] \arrow[dr,"\operatorname{id}_H"'] & E \arrow[d,"r"]\\
& H
\end{tikzcd}
```
